name: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
description: Finds the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. O(n²) DP solution: dp[i] = length of LIS ending at index i.
aim: Find the longest subsequence where every element is strictly greater than the previous one, using dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) for all j<i where arr[j]<arr[i].
howItWorks: Initialize dp[i] = 1 for all i (each element alone is LIS of length 1)
For each i from 1 to n-1:
For each j < i: if arr[j] < arr[i], dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j]+1)
Answer is max(dp[i]) for all i

time.worstCase: All elements decreasing — no early exit

realWorld: Finding longest sorted run in data
alternatives: O(n log n) with patience sort/binary search for large n
